title: Recommendation Feedback Loops Shape Urban Income Segregation and Venue Visitation
abstract: arXiv:2610.41911v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Location-based recommender systems shape where people go in cities and learn from the visits they steer, forming a human-AI feedback loop. This feedback loop shapes whom people share places with across income groups and which venues keep attracting customers. Yet platforms judge these systems by their offline accuracy on past visits, a test in which the suggestions never change where people go and which therefore cannot capture long-term effects. Studying these effects in cities is challenging because, unlike online resources, travel constraints and limited venue capacity shape where people can go, while each recommended visit also changes whom other visitors encounter. To capture such features, we build a long-term simulation framework based on fine-grained human mobility data from four U.S. metropolitan areas, with distance and capacity constraints. translated_title: 推荐反馈循环塑造城市收入隔离与场所访问
translated_abstract: 基于位置的推荐系统塑造着人们在城市中的去向，并从其引导的访问中不断学习，从而形成一个“人-机反馈循环”。这一反馈循环影响着不同收入群体之间共享场所的方式，以及哪些场所能够持续吸引顾客。然而，平台通常以这些系统在历史访问数据上的离线准确率来评价其表现——在这种测试中，推荐永远不会改变人们的实际去向，因此无法捕捉长期效应。在城市情境中研究这些效应颇具挑战性：与在线资源不同，出行距离约束和有限的场所容量限制了人们可以前往的地点，同时每一次被推荐的访问还会改变其他访客可能遇到的人群。为捕捉这些特征，我们基于来自美国四个大都市区的精细化人类移动数据，构建了一个包含距离与容量约束的长期模拟框架。以餐饮场所为研究对象，我们考察了两类城市后果：人们跨收入群体接触（曝光）的不均衡程度……
tldr: 本文构建了一个融合距离与容量约束的长期城市移动模拟框架，揭示推荐系统与人类出行之间形成的反馈循环会加剧跨收入群体的空间隔离，并决定哪些场所能持续吸引客流。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a long-term urban mobility simulation framework with distance and capacity constraints, revealing that the feedback loop between recommender systems and human movement amplifies income segregation and determines which venues keep attracting visitors.
